subject: history
title: The Decolonisation Chain in Southeast Asia
objectives: Explain how independence in one territory raised nationalist pressure in the next
Run the chain in order: Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959
Explain why colonial control fell stage by stage as the chain advanced

definitions.meaning: The ending of colonial rule: in Southeast Asia after the Second World War it advanced territory by territory between 1946 and 1959.
The strength of the campaign for self-rule inside a territory: in the animation it is the bar that rises past the threshold at each stage.
The grip of the colonial power over a territory: in the animation it is the bar that falls stage by stage as the chain advances.
The level of nationalist pressure at which the colonial power concedes: once the pressure bar crosses the line, independence or self-government follows.
The carrying of the example from one territory to the next: campaigners point to a neighbour that has already won, and pressure rises at home.
Control of internal affairs while the colonial power keeps some powers: what Singapore won in 1959, the final stage of this chain.

mechanismSteps: Philippines, 1946: pressure crosses the line - nationalist pressure rises past the threshold, the United States grants independence, the control bar falls and a transmission arrow carries the example on (s1).
Indonesia, 1949: the example raises pressure - Indonesian nationalists point to the Philippine win, pressure rises, and the Netherlands recognises Indonesian independence (s2).
Malaya, 1957: pressure rises, control falls - with two neighbours independent, the pressure bar rises again while the British control bar keeps falling, and Malaya wins independence (s3).
Singapore, 1959: the chain reaches home - campaigners who have watched three neighbours win press their case, and Singapore wins internal self-government (s4).
workedExample: Work through the whole chain in order. Step 1 (s1): Philippines 1946 - pressure crosses the threshold and independence is granted. Step 2 (s2): Indonesia recognised 1949 - the Philippine example raises pressure next door until recognition follows. Step 3 (s3): Malaya 1957 - pressure rises again, now backed by two independent neighbours, and control falls further. Step 4 (s4): Singapore internal self-government 1959 - the chain reaches home. At every stage the order is the same: Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959, and what links them is the carried example, not four separate stories.

trap.misconception: Each colony won independence on its own, because what happened in a neighbouring territory made no difference to nationalist pressure at home.
trap.explanation: The slip: Each independence has its own local leaders, parties and negotiations, so it is easy to treat every territory as a separate story with no connection to its neighbours. The fix: The territories were linked by a chain: independence in one raised nationalist pressure in the next, because campaigners could point to a neighbour that had already won, colonial control weakened stage by stage, and the example was carried on - Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959. In class, replay scene 1: freeze as the Philippine pressure bar crosses the threshold and ask where that example goes next - then run scenes 2 to 4 and watch each transmission arrow land as extra pressure in the neighbouring territory.
